column1: # The thing's own colour. The owner, 6 November: "A bread is brown to me and cheese yellow ... If the category symbols
# carry the real thing in color they would be very recognizable", then, of Groceries drawn so: "Real colors look good".
# A kind whose thing has a colour everyone knows, a food or a drink, wears it wherever Atlas draws its places (places
# KindColours): its pin, its disc in the rows, its chip, its card and its page. Every other kind keeps its family's.
# Each is its thing's colour moved the least it takes, most not at all, so that for every eye it is never taken for
# another family's mark, open or closed, nor for a closed place of its own, and its own closed mark (lighter) still
# shows (FamilyColoursTest). Two kinds may share one, coffee and chocolate both brown: their symbols tell them.
